title: Leviticus Chapter 26 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Leviticus chapter 26 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Leviticus Chapter 26 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Leviticus Chapter 26.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 26:1, what are the Israelites forbidden to make or set up in their land?
questions.correctAnswer: Idols and graven images
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:1 forbids making idols, graven images, or standing images to bow down to in the land.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 26:2 commands the Israelites to keep the sabbaths and reverence the sanctuary.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:2 clearly instructs to keep the sabbaths and reverence the sanctuary.

questions.question: What does God promise to give if the Israelites walk in His statutes and keep His commandments according to Leviticus 26:4?
options: Rain in due season and fruitful trees
questions.correctAnswer: Rain in due season and fruitful trees
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:4 promises rain in due season and that the trees of the field shall yield their fruit if they keep His statutes.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 26:5, what will the Israelites experience regarding their harvests?
options: Threshing will reach vintage and vintage will reach sowing time
They will harvest only once a year
They will have to share with neighbors
questions.correctAnswer: Threshing will reach vintage and vintage will reach sowing time
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:5 states that threshing shall reach unto the vintage and vintage unto the sowing time.

questions.question: Leviticus 26:6 describes God giving peace in the land. What else does He promise about the land?
options: He will rid evil beasts and the sword shall not pass through
The land will be covered with gold
The land will be flooded with water
The land will be filled with strangers
questions.correctAnswer: He will rid evil beasts and the sword shall not pass through
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:6 says God will rid evil beasts and the sword shall not go through the land.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 26:7 says the Israelites will fall before their enemies by the sword.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:7 says the Israelites shall chase their enemies and they shall fall before them by the sword.

questions.question: How many Israelites does Leviticus 26:8 say can chase and put to flight a large number of enemies?
questions.correctAnswer: Five shall chase an hundred
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:8 states that five of you shall chase an hundred, and an hundred shall put ten thousand to flight.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 26:9, what will God do for the Israelites?
options: Make them fruitful and multiply them
questions.correctAnswer: Make them fruitful and multiply them
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:9 says God will have respect unto them, make them fruitful, multiply them, and establish His covenant.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 26:10 states the Israelites shall eat new store and bring forth new because of the old.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:10 says they shall eat old store and bring forth the old because of the new, not the other way around.

questions.question: What does God say He will set among the Israelites according to Leviticus 26:11?
questions.correctAnswer: His tabernacle
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:11 says God will set His tabernacle among them and His soul shall not abhor them.

questions.question: Leviticus 26:12 says God will walk among the Israelites and what else?
options: Be their God and they shall be His people
Make them kings over other nations
questions.correctAnswer: Be their God and they shall be His people
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:12 states God will walk among them, be their God, and they shall be His people.

questions.question: Who does God say He brought the Israelites out of, according to Leviticus 26:13?
questions.correctAnswer: The land of Egypt
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:13 says God brought them out of the land of Egypt.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 26:14 warns that if the Israelites will not hearken to God and do His commandments, blessings will increase.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:14 warns that if they will not hearken and do His commandments, consequences will follow, not blessings.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 26:15, what will happen if the Israelites despise God's statutes and break His covenant?
options: They will face appointed terror and sorrow of heart
They will be given more land
They will become rulers over other nations
questions.correctAnswer: They will face appointed terror and sorrow of heart
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:16 (continuation of 15) says God will appoint terror, consumption, and sorrow of heart if they break the covenant.

questions.question: What is the first punishment God says He will appoint over the Israelites if they break His covenant, according to Leviticus 26:16?
questions.correctAnswer: Terror, consumption, and burning ague
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:16 clearly states God will appoint terror, consumption, and burning ague as punishments.

medium.title: Leviticus Chapter 26 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Leviticus Chapter 26 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 26:17, what will happen when God sets His face against the disobedient?
options: They shall be slain before their enemies and flee when none pursues
They shall find peace and safety in their land
They will receive rain in due season
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be slain before their enemies and flee when none pursues
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:17 states that God will set His face against the disobedient, causing them to be slain before their enemies and to flee even when no one pursues them. This shows the consequences of turning away from God's commandments.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 26:18 say will happen if the people still do not listen after initial punishments?
options: God will punish them seven times more for their sins
They will be given another chance without punishment
They will be blessed with abundant harvests
questions.correctAnswer: God will punish them seven times more for their sins
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:18 clearly states that if the people do not listen after the initial punishment, God will punish them seven times more, emphasizing the seriousness of persistent disobedience.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 26:19 describe the breaking of the people's power as a punishment?
options: Their pride will be broken and their heaven will be like iron, their earth like brass
Their enemies will become their servants
They will become rulers over many nations
Their cities will be filled with peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Their pride will be broken and their heaven will be like iron, their earth like brass
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:19 describes the punishment as breaking the pride of their power and making their heaven like iron and their earth like brass, symbolizing harsh conditions and loss of blessing.

questions.question: What consequence does Leviticus 26:20 mention about the land if the people do not obey God?
options: The land will yield abundant fruit
The land will not yield its increase and trees will not bear fruit
The land will be filled with precious stones
The land will be flooded with water
questions.correctAnswer: The land will not yield its increase and trees will not bear fruit
questions.explanation: According to Leviticus 26:20, disobedience results in the land failing to produce crops and fruit, showing the natural consequences of ignoring God's commandments.

questions.question: Based on Leviticus 26:21-22, what will God send among the people if they walk contrary to Him?
options: Wild beasts that rob children and destroy cattle
questions.correctAnswer: Wild beasts that rob children and destroy cattle
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:21-22 explains that if the people continue to disobey, God will send wild beasts among them to rob their children, destroy their cattle, and make them few in number, illustrating severe judgment.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 26:25 say will happen when God brings a sword upon the people for breaking the covenant?
options: They will be gathered safely in their cities
Pestilence will be sent among them and they will be delivered into the enemy's hand
questions.correctAnswer: Pestilence will be sent among them and they will be delivered into the enemy's hand
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:25 states that when God brings a sword upon the people for breaking the covenant, pestilence will be sent among them and they will be delivered into the hand of the enemy, highlighting the consequences of covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 26:26, what is the significance of ten women baking bread in one oven during times of punishment?
options: It signifies scarcity and rationing of food
It indicates a time of peace and safety
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies scarcity and rationing of food
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:26 describes how ten women will bake bread in one oven and deliver it by weight, illustrating scarcity and rationing during times of divine punishment.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 26:29 describe the extreme consequences of persistent disobedience?
options: They shall eat the flesh of their own sons and daughters
They shall be taken to a land of peace
They shall be blessed with many children
questions.correctAnswer: They shall eat the flesh of their own sons and daughters
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:29 portrays a horrifying consequence of disobedience, where the people shall resort to cannibalism of their own children, emphasizing the gravity of turning away from God.

questions.question: What will God do to the high places and images of the disobedient according to Leviticus 26:30?
options: He will bless them and make them holy
He will destroy the high places, cut down images, and cast their carcasses upon the carcasses of idols
He will multiply their images and sanctuaries
He will hide them from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: He will destroy the high places, cut down images, and cast their carcasses upon the carcasses of idols
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:30 states that God will destroy the high places and images, casting the carcasses upon the carcasses of idols, showing His abhorrence of idolatry and disobedience.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 26:31, what will happen to the cities and sanctuaries of the disobedient?
options: They will flourish and be filled with worshippers
They will be made waste and brought to desolation with no sweet odors
They will be guarded by angels
They will be rebuilt and restored immediately
questions.correctAnswer: They will be made waste and brought to desolation with no sweet odors
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:31 explains that the cities and sanctuaries will be made waste and desolate, and God will not smell the sweet odors, showing His rejection due to disobedience.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 26:32 say about the land and the reaction of enemies?
options: The land will prosper and enemies will flee
The land will be desolate and enemies will be astonished
The land will be divided among the people
Enemies will worship in the land
questions.correctAnswer: The land will be desolate and enemies will be astonished
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:32 tells that God will bring the land into desolation, causing the enemies dwelling there to be astonished, revealing the severity of judgment.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 26:34-35, the land will enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate because the people failed to observe them.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:34-35 states that the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths while desolate because it did not rest during the time when the people dwelt upon it, showing the land's need for rest as commanded by God.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 26:36-37 describes that those left alive will feel faintness in their hearts and fall one upon another even when no one pursues them.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:36-37 describes the fearful condition of those left alive, with faintness and panic causing them to fall one upon another without pursuit, illustrating the deep distress caused by God's judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 26:38 says the people shall perish among the heathen and the land of their enemies shall consume them, indicating complete destruction.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:38 confirms that those who disobey will perish among the heathen and be consumed by the land of their enemies, showing the totality of God's judgment on persistent sin.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 26:40-42 teach about the response of the people when they confess their iniquity?
options: God will forget His covenant with their ancestors
God will remember His covenant with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham and the land
The land will be destroyed forever
questions.correctAnswer: God will remember His covenant with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham and the land
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:40-42 teaches that if the people confess their sins and humble their hearts, God will remember His covenant with their patriarchs and the land, highlighting God's mercy upon repentance.

hard.title: Leviticus Chapter 26 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Leviticus Chapter 26.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 26, what will happen to the land when the Israelites are scattered among the heathen?
options: The land will become fertile and abundant
The land shall be desolate and the cities waste
The land will be given to another nation permanently
The land will prosper under heathen rule
questions.correctAnswer: The land shall be desolate and the cities waste
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:33 states that God will scatter the Israelites among the heathen, and their land shall be desolate and their cities waste as a consequence of their disobedience.

questions.question: What reason does Leviticus 26 give for the land enjoying its sabbaths while desolate?
options: Because the people dedicated it to God
Because it was plowed too much
Because it did not rest in the sabbaths when the Israelites dwelt upon it
Because it was cursed by the nations
questions.correctAnswer: Because it did not rest in the sabbaths when the Israelites dwelt upon it
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:35 explains that the land rests during the desolation period because it failed to rest during the sabbaths while the Israelites inhabited it.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them' in Leviticus 26:36 symbolize about the Israelites' condition in exile?
options: Their fear and faintness causing them to flee at the slightest sound
Their joyful return to the land
The abundance of nature around them
questions.correctAnswer: Their fear and faintness causing them to flee at the slightest sound
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:36 uses this imagery to describe the faintness and fear in the hearts of the exiled Israelites, making them flee even at minor sounds.

questions.question: What consequence is described in Leviticus 26:38 for those Israelites who remain among the heathen?
options: They shall perish, and the land of their enemies shall consume them
They will be honored by the heathen kings
They will prosper in foreign lands
questions.correctAnswer: They shall perish, and the land of their enemies shall consume them
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:38 clearly states that the remaining Israelites will perish among the heathen and be consumed by the land of their enemies.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 26:40-41, what must the Israelites do for God to remember His covenant with them?
options: Build new altars in the heathen lands
Confess their iniquity and humble their uncircumcised hearts
Offer sacrifices to the heathen gods
questions.correctAnswer: Confess their iniquity and humble their uncircumcised hearts
questions.explanation: Verses 40-41 state that confession of iniquity and humbling the uncircumcised heart while accepting punishment are prerequisites for God to remember His covenant.

questions.question: Which patriarchal covenants are recalled by God in Leviticus 26:42 when He promises to remember His covenant with the Israelites?
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:42 mentions God's covenant with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham, affirming His faithfulness despite Israel's failures.

questions.question: What does God declare He will not do to Israel even when they are in the land of their enemies according to Leviticus 26:44?
options: Cast them away or utterly destroy them or break His covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Cast them away or utterly destroy them or break His covenant
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:44 assures that God will not cast away Israel, nor destroy them utterly, nor break His covenant, showing His enduring commitment.

questions.question: Leviticus 26:45 refers to God remembering the covenant He made when bringing the Israelites out of Egypt. Which other Bible passage echoes this theme of God's covenant faithfulness despite Israel’s unfaithfulness?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 31:33-34
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:33-34 speaks of a new covenant and God’s continued faithfulness to Israel despite their sins, echoing the covenant remembrance theme of Leviticus 26:45.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Leviticus 26 to present blessings for obedience and curses for disobedience?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26 uses parallelism by contrasting blessings and curses in a structured way to emphasize consequences of obedience or disobedience (see verses 3-13 and 14-39).

questions.question: In Leviticus 26:29, what extreme punishment is mentioned as a consequence of Israel’s disobedience?
options: They shall eat the flesh of their sons and daughters
questions.correctAnswer: They shall eat the flesh of their sons and daughters
questions.explanation: Verse 29 describes this horrific punishment as part of the curses for Israel’s severe disobedience.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 26:34-35, how long will the land enjoy its sabbaths during Israel’s punishment?
options: As long as it lies desolate
questions.correctAnswer: As long as it lies desolate
questions.explanation: Verses 34-35 explain that the land will rest and enjoy sabbaths as long as it remains desolate because Israel did not allow it to rest.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word translated as 'sabbaths' in Leviticus 26:34-35, and how does it relate to the land?
options: It means 'celebration' and refers to festivals
It means 'rest' and signifies the land’s rest every seventh year
It means 'offering' and relates to sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: It means 'rest' and signifies the land’s rest every seventh year
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Shabbat' means rest or cessation, here referring to the land’s mandated rest during sabbath years (Leviticus 25), which it failed to observe, prompting divine punishment.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 26:37 describe the fate of the Israelites in terms of their power against enemies?
options: They will conquer all enemies easily
They shall fall one upon another and have no power to stand before enemies
They will form alliances with neighboring nations
They will be victorious through prayer
questions.correctAnswer: They shall fall one upon another and have no power to stand before enemies
questions.explanation: Verse 37 illustrates Israel’s helplessness and internal strife, falling before enemies without power to resist.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 26:46 states that these laws and statutes were given by God to the children of Israel through Joshua on Mount Sinai.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:46 specifies that the LORD made these laws through Moses, not Joshua, on Mount Sinai.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 26:44 declares that God will not utterly destroy Israel nor break His covenant with them even when they are in exile among enemies.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:44 affirms God's enduring covenant faithfulness, refusing to cast away or utterly destroy Israel despite their exile.

theological.title: Leviticus Chapter 26 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Leviticus Chapter 26 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 26:4 promise God will provide to the land if Israel walks in His statutes and keeps His commandments?
options: Rain in due season and fruitful trees
The presence of idols and graven images
questions.correctAnswer: Rain in due season and fruitful trees
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:4 states that if Israel obeys God's statutes, He will give rain in due season and the land shall yield its increase, including the trees of the field yielding fruit, demonstrating God's provision and blessing.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily revealed in God's promise to 'walk among you, and will be your God' in Leviticus 26:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Immanence
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:12 reveals God's immanence, His nearness and personal presence among His people, as He promises to walk among them and be their God.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 26:13, what has God done for Israel to establish their identity as His people?
options: Brought them out of Egypt and broke their yoke
Given them wealth and land without struggle
Allowed them to build idols for protection
questions.correctAnswer: Brought them out of Egypt and broke their yoke
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:13 explains that God identifies Himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, freeing them from bondage and breaking their yoke, establishing their covenant relationship with Him.

questions.question: What consequence does God declare in Leviticus 26:16 if Israel despises His statutes and breaks His covenant?
options: Terror, consumption, and burning ague that causes sorrow
questions.correctAnswer: Terror, consumption, and burning ague that causes sorrow
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:16 declares that God will appoint terror, consumption, and burning ague upon Israel if they despise His statutes and break the covenant, showing the serious consequences of disobedience.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 26:21 describe God's response if Israel continues to walk contrary to Him after initial punishments?
options: He will bring seven times more plagues according to their sins
He will immediately restore them without further punishment
He will send angels to protect them
questions.correctAnswer: He will bring seven times more plagues according to their sins
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:21 states that if Israel continues to disobey, God will increase His punishments sevenfold, underscoring the increasing severity of divine judgment for persistent sin.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 26:29 prophesy as one of the dire consequences of Israel's persistent rebellion?
options: Eating the flesh of their sons and daughters
questions.correctAnswer: Eating the flesh of their sons and daughters
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:29 warns of a horrifying judgment where Israel will resort to cannibalism of their own children due to extreme famine and desperation caused by their rebellion.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by God's promise in Leviticus 26:42 to remember His covenant with the patriarchs if Israel confesses their iniquity?
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of Divine Covenant Faithfulness
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:42 teaches that despite Israel's sin, God remains faithful to His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob upon their repentance, highlighting the unbreakable nature of God's covenant promises.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Leviticus 26:11 and 26:12 convey about God's relationship with His people?
options: God dwells among His people and establishes intimate fellowship
God requires sacrifices but no personal relationship
questions.correctAnswer: God dwells among His people and establishes intimate fellowship
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:11 promises God will set His tabernacle among the people and not abhor them, while 26:12 confirms He will walk among them and be their God, together expressing God's desire for intimate fellowship with His covenant people.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by synthesizing Leviticus 26:5-6 and 26:7-8 regarding God's protection and blessing?
options: God blesses with provision and grants victory over enemies
God blesses only with material wealth but not protection
God's protection depends on human strength alone
God allows enemies to triumph as a sign of blessing
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses with provision and grants victory over enemies
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:5-6 promises agricultural blessing and peace, while 26:7-8 assures victory over enemies, together teaching that God's blessing encompasses both material provision and divine protection.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 26:33-34 connect to the broader redemptive narrative concerning Israel's exile and land rest?
options: The land rests during Israel's exile, reflecting consequences of disobedience and anticipation of restoration
Israel's exile means permanent loss of the land without hope
The land remains cursed even after exile ends
The exile is unrelated to the covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: The land rests during Israel's exile, reflecting consequences of disobedience and anticipation of restoration
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:33-34 describes Israel's scattering among nations and land desolation, with the land enjoying sabbaths during exile, illustrating divine discipline and foreshadowing eventual restoration in God's redemptive plan.

questions.question: What attribute of God is emphasized in Leviticus 26:44 where God declares He will not utterly cast away Israel despite their punishment?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy and covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:44 shows God's mercy and faithfulness as He refuses to completely reject Israel, maintaining the covenant relationship despite their sins and punishment.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's punishments in Leviticus 26 are excessively harsh and unjust. What does Leviticus 26:14-17 actually teach about the nature of divine judgment?
options: Judgment is conditional, progressive, and a response to covenant breach
Judgment is arbitrary and without warning
God punishes without chance for repentance
Punishments are unrelated to Israel's behavior
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment is conditional, progressive, and a response to covenant breach
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:14-17 teaches that God's judgments are a direct consequence of Israel's disobedience to the covenant, given progressively with warnings, demonstrating divine justice and covenantal accountability.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth emerges from Leviticus 26:40-42 regarding repentance and God's covenant promises?
options: Repentance leads to God remembering His covenant and restoring His people
Repentance has no effect on God's judgment
God forgets His covenant upon disobedience
Only external rituals, not repentance, restore covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance leads to God remembering His covenant and restoring His people
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:40-42 teaches that when Israel confesses and humbles themselves, God will remember His covenant with the patriarchs and restore them, affirming the power of repentance within the covenant relationship.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 26:22, what is one of the specific judgments God sends among Israel for continued disobedience?
options: Wild beasts that rob children and destroy cattle
questions.correctAnswer: Wild beasts that rob children and destroy cattle
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:22 states that God will send wild beasts among Israel that will rob their children, destroy their cattle, and cause desolation, illustrating the physical and social consequences of sin.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 26:10 emphasize God's providential care even in His blessings?
options: By allowing the consumption of old store because of the new
By forbidding the use of old harvests
By commanding exclusive use of new crops
questions.correctAnswer: By allowing the consumption of old store because of the new
questions.explanation: Leviticus 26:10 highlights God's providence in sustaining His people by allowing them to eat old stored grain as they bring forth new harvests, ensuring continuous provision.
